counterevidence_considered.description: The only candidate structure that could hide a repeated-unit or shared-unit dependence is arena_id, and the analysis independence claims ultimately rest on the description's statement of a single teardown census. However, each arena held exactly one colony (28 distinct arenas for 28 rows), and nothing in the supplied files contradicts the single-census claim, so this does not amount to evidence of repeated independent-unit entry.

source_refs.quoted_text: - arena_id: the sealed flight arena the colony occupied; one arena held one colony.

Independence check: 28 data rows, 28 distinct colony identifiers, 28 distinct arena
identifiers, at most 1 row per colony.

evidence.description: data/input.csv contains exactly 28 data rows with 28 distinct colony_id values (BT-01 through BT-28) and 28 distinct arena_id values; no independent unit appears in more than one row.

The data description names colony_id as the independent-unit column and states that each colony contributes exactly one row with a single lifetime outcome, so a row-independent two-sample test applies to the rows as given.

source_refs.quoted_text: - colony_id: colony label, unique across the file; no colony is entered twice.

Because each colony is measured once and contributes exactly one row, the twenty-eight
rows are twenty-eight independent units, and a row-independent two-sample test applies
directly, with no pooling of within-colony repeats.

evidence.description: The analysis code builds one gyne_count value per row per treatment arm with a simple filter comprehension and passes those lists directly to Welch's t-test; there is no join, expansion, resampling, or replication step that could enter a colony more than once.

The report's own independence check and group tables match the raw data: 28 rows, 28 colonies, at most 1 row per colony, and 14 colonies per arm; the reported means (13.86 and 6.00) reproduce from the raw per-colony gyne counts (sums 194/14 and 84/14), confirming each colony was counted exactly once in the selected Welch t-test result.

source_refs.quoted_text:
Independence check: 28 data rows, 28 distinct colony identifiers, 28 distinct arena
identifiers, at most 1 row per colony.

[selected-result] Welch's two-sided two-sample t-test on lifetime gyne count with one colony per row: control colonies produced 13.86 gynes on average against 6.00 for thiamethoxam-exposed colonies, a difference of 7.86 gynes (t = 4.65, df = 24.5, p < 0.001), so 2 ppb dietary thiamethoxam is associated with markedly reduced gyne output.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by searching for any path through which a colony could enter the two-sample tests more than once: I scanned all 28 CSV data rows for duplicate colony_id or arena_id values (none; BT-01..BT-28 and ARENA-01..ARENA-28 each appear exactly once), checked that per-arm sample sizes (14 + 14) sum to the number of distinct colonies rather than exceeding it, recomputed the arm means from raw counts (control 194/14 = 13.86, exposed 84/14 = 6.00) and the Welch t-statistic (7.86 / sqrt(4.99^2/14 + 3.88^2/14) ≈ 4.65), which match the report and are only consistent with one observation per colony, and inspected analysis.py for any join, concatenation, resampling, or row-expansion step (there is none; rows are read once and filtered by treatment). Every check failed to produce the issue.
